rules.title: Every departure from PHP's observable behaviour is listed as a divergence, and each exists only because PHP left a binding untyped
rules.divergesFromPhp: the imported `.phpt` corpus passes at a structurally lower rate than a compatibility-first design would, and a failure in a listed class is intentional rather than a regression

rules.title: `->` on a receiver that can hold no object is refused where it is written
rules.divergesFromPhp: `$i->name` on an `int` is a compile error (`E0495`) rather than a warning yielding `null`; only `mixed` keeps PHP's run-time answer, through a name-keyed fetch that throws

rules.title: Absent storage never reads as a zero value: an unassigned variable and `[]` in a read position are refused, and an absent key throws
rules.divergesFromPhp: reading an undefined variable or an absent array key does not warn and yield `null`, and `$a[] .= "x"` does not append; `??`, `isset` and `empty` keep PHP's answer

rules.title: An element write through a temporary is refused, because the separated copy has nowhere to be written back
rules.divergesFromPhp: `f()[0] = 2` is `E0700` rather than a silently discarded write, and `(new Box())->rows[0] = 2` is accepted where PHP 8.5 refuses it

rules.title: A non-`void` body hands back a value at every exit; nothing returns `null` for a declaration it did not make
rules.divergesFromPhp: a body that falls off its end is `E0739` and a written `return;` under a non-`void` declaration is `E0822`, each where it stands rather than a `null` return or a `TypeError` at run time

rules.title: A `return` never leaves a `finally` block, and neither does a `break` or `continue` whose target lies outside it
rules.divergesFromPhp: `return` inside `finally` does not compile, instead of overriding the region's result and discarding a throw in flight (deprecated in 8.6)

rules.title: A constructor's `return` carries no value; a bare `return;` may still leave early
rules.divergesFromPhp: `return $value;` in a constructor does not compile (deprecated in 8.6)

rules.title: A `readonly` property declares no default; a value known at the declaration is a `const`
rules.divergesFromPhp: `readonly int $n = 1;` is refused where PHP 8.6 allows it

rules.title: Partial function application is not adopted; the closure literal already spells it
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP 8.6's `f(?, $x)` does not parse; write `fn($a) => f($a, $x)`

rules.title: `let` and `is` cannot name anything; `var` declares, `as` converts, and `is` is the type test
rules.divergesFromPhp: `let` and `is` cannot name anything (deprecated as identifiers in 8.6), so a converted program renames them

rules.title: `instanceof` is refused where it is written, `is` is the one type test, and neither keyword is compared with PHP again
rules.divergesFromPhp: PHP keeps `instanceof` beside the `is` it has reserved; Novis refuses the spelling outright and names the rewrite, and gives `$x is $cls` the dynamic class test PHP's Pattern Matching RFC leaves unclaimed

rules.title: What PHP deprecates for removal is refused at compile time, never phased in behind a warning
rules.divergesFromPhp: a PHP 8.6 deprecation is a compile error at the line it is written, with no deprecation channel and no warning

rules.title: `nvs convert` turns a stateless trait into an interface with defaults and a stateful one into a delegate, and names what it cannot decide
rules.divergesFromPhp: `use T;` becomes `implements T`, a trait with state becomes a `{Trait}Impl` delegate flagged for review, and a trait `static` or a callback into the consuming class is a `TODO`

rules.title: `nvs convert` maps every PHP shell-execution call to `Core\Process` and flags each site, because a command string has no argv split
rules.divergesFromPhp: `exec`, `system`, backticks, `shell_exec`, `passthru` and `proc_open` all become `Core\Process::run` or `spawn`, with a human supplying the executable path and the argv

rules.title: A session id the store did not issue is rejected, always, with no toggle
rules.divergesFromPhp: `session.use_strict_mode` has no off position: an unknown, expired or attacker-minted id is discarded and a fresh one issued

rules.title: The PHP-name layer is joined once at build time, and a destination spelling the registry cannot place fails the build
Every PHP built-in name is a completion candidate, and the migration table is what the item says
rules.divergesFromPhp: typing the PHP name you already know completes to the Novis member, and the PHP spelling never reaches a file

rules.title: A PHP-name completion item inserts only a `Core` member the registry already holds
rules.divergesFromPhp: a suggestion whose destination is dropped, undecided or not built yet appears and inserts nothing, where a PHP editor completes any name it has indexed

rules.title: A PHP name completes only where a top-level identifier is legal, and sorts below every Novis symbol
rules.divergesFromPhp: the PHP name is the fallback rather than the first suggestion, and it never appears after a receiver or a `::`

rules.title: `nvs.completion.phpNames` quiets or removes the PHP-name layer, and never touches `Core` completion
rules.divergesFromPhp: the setting removes a reminder layer, never a spelling — no PHP name is ever an alias the program can reach
